answers.bix-10-q1: In the multivariable ordinal logistic regression including BCG status, expected interaction, and patient volume (patients_seen_code), the odds ratio for higher COVID-19 severity for BCG vs placebo is 1.52.
answers.bix-10-q2: In the ordered logit model adjusting for patients_seen_code and BCG status, the odds ratio for higher COVID-19 severity for healthcare workers expecting to interact with patients (Yes vs No) is 0.75.
answers.bix-10-q3: A statistically significant difference (p<0.05) in COVID-19 severity between BCG and placebo is observed in the 1–50 patients seen group (p ≈ 0.024).
answers.bix-10-q4: Among workers who expect to interact with patients, the chi-square test p-value for association between BCG vaccination and COVID-19 severity is approximately 0.025.
answers.bix-10-q5: For healthcare workers seeing over 100 patients, the chi-square test p-value for the association between vaccination status and disease severity is approximately 0.44.
answers.bix-10-q6: For healthcare workers seeing 1–50 patients, the chi-square test p-value for the association between vaccination status and disease severity is approximately 0.024.
answers.bix-10-q7: The odds ratio for higher COVID-19 severity for those expecting to interact with patients vs those who do not is 0.75, corresponding to about a 24.5% reduction in odds after controlling for BCG vaccination and number of patients seen.
